head: """Steam game install/launch via deeplink + appid resolution.
This tool sidesteps the GUI-automation problem for Steam entirely:
Old approach: deeplink to Steam library → snapshot UIA tree → search game →
click listitem → snapshot again → find Install button → click. Many steps,
fragile because Steam UI is CEF-rendered and the React layer changes views
out of sync with what `gui(snapshot)` reads.
New approach (researched 2026-05-11):
1. Resolve "Doom Eternal" → appid 782330 via:
a) Local appmanifest_*.acf files (offline, if user owns the game).
b) Steam Store search API `store.steampowered.com/api/storesearch/`
(online, no key required, ~200ms).
2. Dispatch `steam://rungameid/<appid>` — this single URI:
- launches the game if installed
- starts download + launch if owned but not installed
- falls back to store page if not owned
This is the standard Steam protocol behavior, validated against Valve's
official browser protocol wiki + community testing. No GUI clicks needed
for the common case.
References:
- Valve Wiki: https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Steam_browser_protocol
- Steamworks IStoreService: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/IStoreService
- Steam community thread on URI behavior: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/540744935066349428/

head: """Windows UIA snapshot — serializes accessibility tree to text with stable refs.
Port of openclaw's browser ARIA-tree-as-text pattern
(extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.ts + chrome-mcp.snapshot.ts), but for
Windows native apps via Microsoft UI Automation (UIA).
The idea — already validated in production by openclaw with Gemma 4:
Instead of feeding screenshots to the LLM and asking it to "see" buttons,
we serialize the OS-level accessibility tree to plain text:
- Window "Steam"
- tabitem "Library" [ref=e1]
- text "Doom Eternal"
- button "Install" [ref=e42]
- button "Buy" [ref=e43]
The LLM (Gemma 4) reads this text, decides `act(ref="e42")`, and we
resolve `e42` back to the real UIA element to invoke its click pattern.
Why this works on Gemma 4:
- LLM plays to its strength (text comprehension)
- No pixel reasoning, no coordinates, no VLM needed
- Refs are stable — `e42` resolves the same element until the snapshot is
superseded by a new one
- Compact: an interactive-only Steam page is ~50 lines, vs the OCR text
extraction which is hundreds of lines of noise
This module mirrors openclaw's chrome-mcp.snapshot.ts:flattenChromeMcpSnapshotToAriaNodes
and buildAiSnapshotFromChromeMcpSnapshot logic, adapted to UIA's role taxonomy.

head: """Verifiers runtime post-call para confirmar efectos reales de tools.
Valor 4 ContextoCarter: una tool reportar ok=True NO es suficiente; el
agent debe leer el estado real del sistema y declarar status.
Diferencia vs verify.py:
- verify.py tiene `@register_verifier(tool_name)` que se llama DENTRO
del registry de Carter (acoplado a las tools individuales). Lo usan
los handlers reales para reportar VerifierOutcome al orchestrator.
- verify_runtime.py es la capa runtime adicional: status enum
COMPLETED/UNVERIFIED/PARTIAL/BLOCKED que el agent loop puede mergear
en el result que retorna al modelo en el next turn. Usa pycaw para
audio, tasklist para procesos, Path para filesystem. Independiente
del registry — útil cuando una tool composite no preserva el verifier
de la individual.
Status enum:
COMPLETED:  efecto medido y confirmado.
UNVERIFIED: no se pudo medir (dep faltante, tool reportó error).
PARTIAL:    medido pero divergencia menor (tolerable).
BLOCKED:    sistema rechazó la operacion (UAC, permission denied).

import time

return {"status": "COMPLETED", "evidence": evidence, "reason": ""}
def _u(reason: str, evidence: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict:
return {"status": "UNVERIFIED", "evidence": evidence or {}, "reason": reason}
